snippets.why_me_120w: I came back to Bihar after Cambridge with a research framework and no technology. A decade later I have the technology but still no grants team, no comms team, and no AI budget. Everything I have built — Rusty, Suchi Cancer Bot, the funding assistant — has been built to solve that gap: giving small, deeply-rooted organisations the same tools that well-funded ones take for granted. I am not researching AI for social good from the outside. I am deploying it, iterating it against real beneficiaries in Bihar government schools and cancer wards, and learning what actually works when connectivity is low, literacy is mixed, and the stakes are real.
snippets.my_work_200w: I run two organisations from Patna, Bihar. Diksha Foundation (founded 2010) operates KHEL centres — hybrid education hubs combining digital literacy, Football3 sports coaching, and social-emotional learning — serving 476 children directly and 511 through government school partnerships. Empowering Futures reaches ~260 adolescent girls across urban Patna. Suchitra Cancer Care Foundation (founded 2024, named after my mother) builds cancer navigation tools for patients and families. Its flagship product, Suchi Cancer Bot, answers cancer questions in plain language and guides families through the healthcare system. Across both organisations I am building AI infrastructure that replaces what a 10-person team would otherwise do: a WhatsApp tutor (Rusty, piloted with 70 Bihar Board students via Glific), a cancer navigation bot, a KB-backed grants assistant that researches funders, scores fit, and drafts proposals. The goal is operational parity — so that a Bihar-based NGO with three staff can compete for funding and deliver programs with the same quality as an organisation ten times its size.
snippets.ai_story_200w: My AI journey started not with excitement but with frustration. In 2023, I watched Diksha lose a grant we were well-suited for because we submitted a generic proposal. We didn't have time to research the funder properly. We didn't have a grants writer. The winning organisation did. I started building the funding assistant to solve that specific problem — not as a product, but as internal infrastructure. It now researches funders via web grounding, retrieves evidence from our KB using pgvector, scores fit across six dimensions, and drafts full proposals with citations. We used it to generate our first Reliance Foundation ESA proposal in under 10 minutes. Then came Rusty — a WhatsApp tutor for Bihar Board students built with Glific, because our students don't have laptops or stable internet but they do have phones and WhatsApp. Then Suchi Cancer Bot — because cancer patients in Bihar are navigating a terrifying system with no information and no guide. What connects all three is the same design principle: AI that works within the actual constraints of the people it serves — low bandwidth, mixed literacy, no budget — rather than the constraints of people who can afford to ignore those things.
snippets.bio_50w: Gautam Gauri is Executive Director of Diksha Foundation, a Bihar-based education NGO he co-founded in 2010, and co-founder of Suchitra Cancer Care Foundation. He holds an MPhil in Education from Cambridge (2016) and builds AI tools — including a WhatsApp tutor, a cancer navigation bot, and a grants assistant — for under-resourced communities.
snippets.bio_100w: Gautam Gauri co-founded Diksha Foundation in 2010, building holistic education programs for over 2,000 children in Bihar through KHEL centres integrating digital literacy, football-for-development, and social-emotional learning. In 2024 he co-founded Suchitra Cancer Care Foundation — named after his mother — to build patient navigation and cancer education tools. He holds an MPhil in Education from the University of Cambridge (2015-16). Since 2024 he has been building a suite of AI tools: Rusty (WhatsApp tutor for Bihar Board learners), Suchi Cancer Bot (cancer navigation assistant), and a funding assistant that helps both organisations compete for grants they would otherwise lose to larger, better-resourced organisations.
snippets.bio_200w: Gautam Gauri co-founded Diksha Foundation in Patna, Bihar in 2010. Over 15 years, Diksha has reached 2,000+ children through its KHEL (Knowledge Hub for Education and Learning) programme — a hub-and-spoke model integrating digital literacy, Football3 sports coaching, and SEE Learning across 3 centres and 10 government school spokes in Bihar. He also leads Empowering Futures, reaching ~260 adolescent girls across 6 urban settlements in Patna. In 2024, following the loss of his mother Suchitra, he co-founded Suchitra Cancer Care Foundation to build patient navigation and cancer education tools for families who face cancer diagnoses without guidance or resources. The foundation's flagship product, Suchi Cancer Bot, provides 24/7 cancer information and navigation in plain language. Gautam holds an MPhil in Education from the University of Cambridge (2015-16), where his research focused on the Capabilities Approach to education. Since returning to India, he has worked at the intersection of education, technology, and social equity in Bihar — one of India's most under-served states. Since 2024, he has been building AI tools — Rusty (WhatsApp-native tutor for Bihar Board students), Suchi Cancer Bot, and a funding automation system — specifically designed for organisations with no resources to pay for them.
